There is an example in the spec that shows how the .font attribute works.  I think you should add another example that shows how to do it in workers (including the font loading).

Also, I see that the css font loading spec already states that WorkerGlobalScope implements FontFaceSource, which is great, but I wonder whether there is anything in this spec that is necessary to make the right connection to the FontFaceSource.  Maybe nothing is needed, I'm just not sure. WDYT?
I think it's fine. There's a notion of `"font style source object"` which includes the object context in which the font is resolved.
Ping @whatwg/canvas again. Unfortunately we have an issue with a bot that precludes OP from pinging teams.

It seems you also need to change where `TextMetrics` is exposed, right?

We should probably also make it more clear that "font style source object" is not always available and make all its accessors clearly branch on it.

And to be sure, all of this will work in service workers?

Done `TextMetrics`.

My idea was: to make OffscreenCanvas itself the "font style source object", which means it gets the default properties of an object as a fallback. Does that work?

It does work on service workers.

I'm not sure what the default properties of an object would be, but maybe?

It seems one of the problems here is that the current setup only supports the `ltr` direction in workers. That doesn't really seem acceptable.
Why do you say that? Doesn't context.direction solves this?
Yeah, it totally does, my bad.
@annevk can you help me bringing other folks attention to this and #3677 ? I've tried to tag a few folks there, but not sure what else to do.
High-level LGTM from my standpoint. Will be good to get this functionality into workers.
@jdashg could you give feedback? Thanks.
This seems like a reasonable extension of Canvas to OffscreenCanvas. LGTM
Tests: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/11362
WPT is in. @annevk is this good to go?

> make OffscreenCanvas itself the "font style source object"

That isn't clear yet, is it?

This also needs browser bugs as per https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/master/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests.

@annevk re the source object, I think it is. :) Could you PTAL?

Working on the bugs now.

Implementation bugs:

[Edge](https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/platform/issues/17934327/)
[Firefox](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1469281)
[Safari](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=186759)
It's already implemented on Chrome, but here's the [bug](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=722393).
So how is the font style source object's fonts object determined? Apart from that it does indeed seem fine.
Doesn't line 60931 addresses that? For `OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D` it's `OffscreenCanvas`.

That gives you the "font style source object". But that object supposedly has a "font source" (sorry for getting the name wrong earlier):

> (Each font style source object has a font source, which determines what fonts are available.)

Ahn, that's right. This is already partially covered by the FontSet spec. But I think it's worth specing the behavior for offscreencanvas: the font source is the document or the workerglobalscope, depending on the hosting object of the offscreencanvas. I'll add this.

On a second look, I think this is already properly defined.
By `CSSFONTLOAD`:
```
Any document, workers, or other context which can use fonts in some manner must implement
the FontFaceSource interface. The value of the context’s fonts attribute is its font 
source, which provides all of the fonts used in font-related operations, unless defined 
otherwise. Operations referring to “the font source” must be interpreted as referring to 
the font source of the relevant context in which the operation is taking place.
```

Right?
That seems quite hand-wavy and for documents it's probably not precise enough as you can have a lot of documents and it's not immediately obvious how one is obtained here.

I agree is a bit hand wavy. But for `document`, the situation is already as is, right? And for the worker it seems pretty straightforward to me.

I'll add a separate paragraph making a bit more explicit the font source for `OffscreenCanvas` then.
Done. PTAL.

@fserb, please take a look at my changes, to confirm they are all editorial. Things to note for future edits:

- Be sure to properly reference well-defined terms, like "node document", "relevant global object", "associated Document", "associated OffscreenCanvas object", and "canvas attribute". Those have precise definitions, whereas the previous versions ("owning `Document`", "the global object", "the `document` object", "the `OffscreenCanvas` object", and "the canvas property") were not defined anywhere. Unfortunately we don't have a compiler to check for such "undefined variable references" in an automated fashion, but hopefully you'll see the pattern.
- If you scan the rest of the spec, you'll find that references (i.e. `<ref spec=...>`) always appear at the end of a paragraph, not at the end of a sentence. I've updated to be consistent with that style.
- The way of determining the "font source" was getting confusing in paragraph form, so I refactored it to an algorithm. Hopefully this more closely mirrors what you would implement.
- It wasn't clear what "font source" was derived from: the font style source object, or the CanvasTextDrawingStyles object, or whether it was global for the whole user agent, or... I made it explicitly a function of the CanvasTextDrawingStyles object, since it seems like you need that information to figure out the answer. I hope that was correct.
Hmm it seems like @junov's suggestion to add an example, in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/3708#issuecomment-391481831, was not addressed. @fserb can you do that?

The algorithm LGTM.
Added an example code.

Yes. Right here: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/3708#issuecomment-398048761
